title: Effect ledger projection (RFC 0173 §C.2)
description: GET /runs/{runId}/effects — the Layer-2 effect records keyed on business identity (the activity recipe is the documented fallback). Content-free of provider payloads.

providerKey.description: Redaction-safe provider-side identity (RFC 0150); never credential material.

state.description: The attempt's lifecycle state. The enum is the VOCABULARY a host must label attempts with, not a set of states every host must produce: a host emits the states its own effect lifecycle actually reaches, and one that only claims and completes attempts emits only `claimed` and `completed`. Both floor scenarios that read this projection witness attempt EXISTENCE and identity — `v2-effect-seam-no-refire` checks that a replay fork records no attempt the parent did not make (by `nodeId`/`attempt`/`at`) and `v2-effect-identity-business-key` reads `effectId`/`providerKey` across attempts; neither reads `state`. So a two-state ledger is schema-valid and witness-sufficient, and `released`/`escaped` are projection surface for operators rather than witness surface for the suite. What a host MUST NOT do is record only exceptional attempts: a ledger that writes a row only when an effect ESCAPES leaves a correctly-suppressed effect invisible, and suppression is then unwitnessable — the no-re-fire scenario records `blocked` on an empty source ledger rather than passing on 0 == 0.

cacheKey.description: RFC 0260 §C (normative home). A host advertising replay.llmCacheKeyRecipe MUST carry this on every LLM provider-call record made while advertised; no preimage. On replay a recorded result is served only to an invocation whose key, by the recipe the record names, equals digest; a record without cacheKey is matched by the RFC 0041 recipe; a fork copies cacheKey verbatim.
